Analyst Emmanuel Papadakis argued that Novartis
stock has climbed since the Q3 report, which showed an earnings miss driven by a $2.2B charge for experimental drugs del-desiran and pelacarsen following their late-stage trial setbacks last month.

“With the stock now having more than retraced losses since the misses on pelacarsen and del desiran, it is starting to look a little incongruous,” Papadakis wrote as he cut his price target to CHF115 from CHF120 per share.
The analyst argues that he fails to see a base case scenario in which Novartis
avoids a patent cliff for its breast cancer therapy, Kisqali, in 2031, and adds that the company lacks key clinical events for next year.
